name: Fleurieu

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
